title: How much continuing education does an investment adviser representative need each year?
description: NASAA's IAR CE model rule: 12 credits a year (6 ethics, 6 products and practice), the 25 adopting jurisdictions, CE Inactive status and FINRA overlap.
shortAnswer: Investment adviser representatives registered in a state that has adopted the North American Securities Administrators Association (NASAA) model rule on IAR continuing education must complete 12 credits each calendar year: 6 credits of Ethics and Professional Responsibility and 6 credits of Products and Practice, from NASAA-approved providers. As at November 2026, NASAA lists 25 adopting jurisdictions. Missing the requirement leads to CE Inactive status and, after a second year, loss of registration eligibility.
keyTakeaways: NASAA adopted the IAR CE model rule on November 24, 2020; each state brings it into force through its own securities rules, effective January 1 of a stated year.
The annual requirement is 12 credits split 6 and 6, and the split is strict: 8 Products and Practice plus 4 Ethics does not satisfy the year. A credit is at least 50 minutes of instruction.
The requirement follows where the representative is registered, not where the firm is registered or notice filed, and it applies to IARs of both state-registered and SEC-registered advisers.
Dual registrants who complete FINRA's Regulatory Element can apply it to the 6 Products and Practice credits; the Ethics credits must still come from approved IAR CE content.
Credits do not carry forward, a repeated course does not count, and an unmet year accumulates as a deficiency of up to 36 credits that follows the individual into any adopting state.
jurisdiction: United States (state securities regulation; 25 jurisdictions listed by NASAA as at November 2026)
regulator: State securities regulators in each adopting jurisdiction, coordinating through the North American Securities Administrators Association (NASAA); the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA) tracks completions in the Central Registration Depository
appliesTo: Investment adviser representatives registered in an adopting jurisdiction, for state-registered investment advisers
Investment adviser representatives of SEC-registered (federal covered) advisers who are registered in an adopting jurisdiction
Dually registered representatives who are also FINRA broker-dealer agents
Investment adviser firms that supervise representatives and track their registration status

sections.heading: What does the NASAA IAR CE model rule require?

blocks.text: The model rule requires every registered investment adviser representative (IAR) to complete 6 credits of Ethics and Professional Responsibility content and 6 credits of Products and Practice content in each reporting period, from an authorized provider. NASAA adopted the [Model Rule on Investment Adviser Representative Continuing Education](https://www.nasaa.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/NASAA-IAR-CE-Model-Rule.pdf) on November 24, 2020, as Model Rule 2002-411(h) or 1956-204(b)(6)-CE, so it can slot into states using either Uniform Securities Act.

blocks.title: Model rule, subrule (1)(A)
blocks.text: "An investment adviser representative must complete six (6) Credits of IAR Regulatory and Ethics Content offered by an Authorized Provider, with at least three (3) hours covering the topic of ethics."

The rule defines a credit as at least 50 minutes of educational instruction and a reporting period as one 12 month period set by NASAA, which NASAA's [IAR CE FAQ](https://www.nasaa.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/IAR-CE-FAQs.pdf) confirms is the calendar year. NASAA requires every approved Ethics and Professional Responsibility course to devote at least half its material to ethical responsibility, so completing all 6 credits automatically meets the 3 hour ethics floor. Representatives choose their own approved courses; the rule does not assign a curriculum.

sections.heading: Who is covered, and which jurisdictions have adopted it?

blocks.text: The requirement applies to every IAR registered in an adopting jurisdiction, whether their firm is state-registered or registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). NASAA's FAQ stresses that the trigger is where the individual is registered, "regardless of where the IAR is domiciled or the firm is registered or notice filed." The model rule's definition of IAR includes anyone meeting the SEC's definition in [17 CFR 275.203A-3](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/chapter-II/part-275/section-275.203A-3).

blocks.text: NASAA's list is based on what jurisdictions have "informed NASAA", so a firm should confirm with each state regulator before relying on it. Under the FAQ, the requirement begins on January 1 of the year following adoption, and a representative registering in an adopting state for the first time has no requirement until January 1 of the next full calendar year. Indiana's requirement is listed as effective in 2027 and does not bind Indiana-only representatives as at November 2026.

sections.heading: Does FINRA continuing education count toward IAR CE?

blocks.text: Partly. A representative who is also a FINRA broker-dealer agent and complies with FINRA's continuing education is treated as meeting the 6 Products and Practice credits, under subrule (2) of the model rule, but not the 6 Ethics credits. The FINRA requirements themselves are covered in [FINRA continuing education requirements](/regulations/finra-continuing-education-requirements).

The credit is not automatic. NASAA's guidance says the Regulatory Element completion must be reported to the IAR CE record, either by the broker-dealer or by the representative through FINRA's [Financial Professional Gateway (FinPro)](https://www.finra.org/registration-exams-ce/finpro), with a reporting fee of $18 ($3 per credit for 6 credits). NASAA's FAQ also allows FINRA Maintaining Qualifications Program CE to be applied the same way. Separately, continuing education required to maintain a credential that qualifies for an exam waiver can satisfy both components if the credentialing body's content is approved IAR CE content (subrule (3)).

sections.heading: What happens if an IAR misses the annual requirement?

blocks.text: The representative renews as "CE Inactive" at year end, and if still CE Inactive at the close of the following year is not eligible for registration or renewal. That two-step consequence is in subrule (6) of the model rule. NASAA notes that completions must appear in the Central Registration Depository (CRD) before FINRA's annual CRD System Shutdown Date to count for that year's processing.

items: **No carry-forward:** excess credits in one year cannot be applied to a later year (subrule (5)).
**Make-up rules:** credits completed in a year apply first to any prior year's deficiency, then to the current year.
**Duplicates:** a course with the same course identifier does not count twice, even in a later year.

**The deficiency travels:** once an individual has been registered in an adopting state for any part of a year, an unmet requirement keeps accruing, up to 36 credits, and affects future registrations in adopting states.
**Unregistered periods:** a returning representative must make up CE for the gap unless they retake the qualifying exam or receive an exam waiver (subrule (9)).

blocks.text: A home state reciprocity provision (subrule (8)) treats a representative as compliant if their home state's requirements are at least as stringent and they meet them. Administrators also have a discretionary waiver power (subrule (7)), which NASAA describes as usually reserved for extraordinary circumstances and effective only in the state that grants it.

sections.heading: How should an adviser firm track IAR CE and evidence it?

blocks.text: The firm's job is to know which representatives are registered in adopting states, confirm completions are actually reported to CRD before the shutdown date, and catch dual registrants whose Regulatory Element credit has not been applied. sections.heading: How does IAR CE fit with other US financial services licensing education?

blocks.text: IAR CE is a registration maintenance requirement for individuals, separate from any firm-level compliance training an adviser runs under its own policies. Many advisory staff hold several licenses at once, so the same person may also owe insurance producer education (see [insurance producer continuing education](/regulations/insurance-producer-continuing-education-requirements)) or, less often, mortgage originator education under the SAFE Act.

Each regime has its own credit definitions, deadlines and no-repeat rules, which is why a single annual course rarely satisfies more than one. NASAA's FAQ notes that some approved courses are also approved for professional designations, but the provider must report the completion to FINRA for it to appear on the IAR CE transcript. More on the sector's obligations is on the [financial services industry page](/industries/financial-services).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry records each representative's registrations, the requirements each one triggers and the content categories that satisfy them, so ethics, products and practice, FINRA and designation credits are mapped before courses are selected. Gaps such as an unapplied Regulatory Element credit or a registration in a newly adopting state show up as framework gaps rather than year-end surprises.

faqs.q: Is IAR CE required in every US state?
faqs.a: No. It applies only in jurisdictions that have adopted the NASAA model rule. As at November 2026 NASAA lists 25, from Maryland, Mississippi and Vermont in 2022 to Illinois in 2026, with Indiana listed for 2027. A representative registered in several states is bound if any one of them has adopted it.

faqs.q: Can an IAR take 12 credits of any approved content?
faqs.a: No. The 12 credits must be split 6 Ethics and Professional Responsibility and 6 Products and Practice. NASAA's FAQ gives the example that 8 Products and Practice credits plus 4 Ethics credits do not satisfy the year, even though they total 12.

faqs.q: Do self-study and online courses count for IAR CE?
faqs.a: Yes, if NASAA has approved the course. NASAA's FAQ states there is no cap on credits earned through self-study or similar formats. Since August 1, 2023, live instructor-led courses must offer an opportunity for audience engagement instead of an assessment.

faqs.q: Can an IAR who teaches an approved course earn credit?
faqs.a: Yes. NASAA's FAQ allows instructors who are IARs to earn credit for courses they teach, but only once for each unique approved course they lead.
